plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a HfO2/MgF2 quarter-wave stack with cavity-defect tuning can achieve the required UV bandpass with visible/NIR suppression. The design draws from recalled knowledge of UV-compatible dielectric pairs and Fabry-Pérot filter physics. I would have wanted to look up actual n/k dispersion data for HfO2 and MgF2 below 300 nm to confirm low absorption in the 255-280 nm band, and to verify deposition stress limits for 29-layer stacks on fused silica.

routes.title: HfO2/MgF2 Quarter-Wave Stack with QWOT-Seeded Thickness Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack with quarter-wave optical thickness seeding at 267.5 nm center wavelength, followed by gradient-based thickness tuning, will produce higher target scores than random initialization while maintaining physical validity across all three spectral bands.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high reflectance outside the passband through constructive interference of reflected waves. A central cavity defect (thickened layer) breaks the periodicity to create a transmission peak. Starting from QWOT values anchors the search near Fabry-Pérot resonance conditions, reducing optimization iterations needed to find valid candidates.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | fused silica substrate (29 film layers total, alternating high/low index starting with HfO2)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers with QWOT seeding at 267.5 nm center wavelength and ±15% multiplicative noise initialization
soft_objectives: maintain physical validity (no negative thicknesses, no absorption violations)
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 29 to stay under 30-layer limit
HfO2 and MgF2 are both conventional e-beam evaporable dielectrics
fused silica substrate matches space platform optical window material
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: HfO2/MgF2 is a standard UV-compatible high/low index pair with sufficient contrast for bandpass filters
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave optical thickness at band center creates maximum reflectance outside the passband
Recalled knowledge: Cavity defects in periodic stacks create transmission peaks at designed wavelengths
Recalled knowledge: QWOT seeding reduces optimization search space compared to random initialization
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has low absorption down to ~120 nm, making it suitable for 255-280 nm operation
expected_advantages: QWOT seeding should produce higher initial valid candidate counts than random initialization
Gradient optimization from physics-aware starting point should converge faster
29-layer count provides sufficient degrees of freedom for three-band spectral control
HfO2/MgF2 pair is well-established for UV applications from recalled deposition practice
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 absorption remains low enough at 255 nm - would need to check actual k values from material registry
Uncertain whether 29 layers can be deposited without excessive stress on fused silica - would need coating stress data
Uncertain whether quarter-wave design at 267.5 nm optimally balances the 255-280 nm band - center wavelength choice is a hypothesis
No literature verification of this exact stack configuration for solar-blind UV applications
Refractive index dispersion below 300 nm may differ from extrapolated values - material registry data quality is unknown to me
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 29-layer planar multilayer thin-film filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating HfO2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers starting with HfO2 adjacent to air, ending with HfO2 adjacent to substrate (15 HfO2 layers, 14 MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers). Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness at 267.5 nm center wavelength (thickness_i = 267.5 nm / (4 * n_i) where n_i is the refractive index of layer material i), then apply ±15% multiplicative noise to create initial population diversity. Optimize all 29 individual layer thicknesses using gradient-based methods to maximize transmission in 255-280 nm band while minimizing transmission in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Total film layers must equal exactly 29. No metal layers allowed. Materials must be hfo2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) only for film layers, SiO2 (Gao) for substrate. Evaluate at normal incidence unless otherwise specified in solver defaults.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation round implementing QWOT-seeded initialization per feedback directive: replaced random initialization with physics-aware quarter-wave optical thickness seeding at bandpass center wavelength with ±15% multiplicative noise to anchor search near Fabry-Pérot resonance conditions while preserving population diversity.

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route cannot achieve best_target_score above 0.4 after QWOT-seeded optimization, the fundamental HfO2/MgF2 pair choice or 29-layer topology may be unsuitable for this three-band spectral requirement, and material pair or layer count axes would need to be explored in separate routes.

valid_candidates count should increase in early rounds due to physics-aware initialization reducing physically invalid configurations
tightest_margin should not fall systematically across rounds if QWOT seeding maintains design robustness
thicknesses_nm should converge toward values near QWOT baseline with localized deviations for band shaping
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops to zero for two consecutive rounds, relax the ±15% noise bound to ±25% and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.1 for three consecutive rounds, reduce optimization step size and continue

Rank 1 is the most physically reliable candidate. Use the highest-ranked candidate that also satisfies the user's exact material formula, state and source constraints. selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
